predictions.prompt: What does RECALL currently remember for this project? Show me the main IDs and categories.
Audit my RECALL memory for stale or noisy entries before I clean it up.
List active RECALL memories from the requirements category and include their IDs.
Before I prune anything, gather the memory IDs that look like archive candidates.
Check whether the recent heavy tool-use session polluted RECALL with low-value command memories.
Save this implementation decision as a new durable memory.
Search memory for the database migration topic I mentioned last week.
Summarize the current repository architecture from the source files.
Audit this code review for noisy comments and conflicting suggestions.

orchestration.reasoning: The skill is a focused inspection workflow with a clear non-mutating contract, concrete command path, expected inputs, filters, result handling, and handoff boundaries to manage-memory. It is composable and mostly explicit. The main weakness is some ambiguity around locating the installed/source plugin root and reliance on related sibling skills that are referenced but not specified here.
evidence: Defines inspection-only ownership and explicitly forbids mutation or new-memory capture.
Specifies public adapter commands and warns not to use lower-level backend scripts.
Provides inputs, filters, workflow steps, output format, troubleshooting, and handoff guidance.
Contract is slightly dependent on external sibling skills and plugin-root resolution, which may require context not included in the skill text.

simulations.task: User asks: 'What does RECALL currently know about this project?'
simulations.expected_output: Codex would run review-memory with a default limit, then return a compact summary with scope, counts, key IDs, and follow-up recommendations without dumping all records.
simulations.quality_notes: The instructions are sufficient and likely produce a useful answer. The only gap is that the skill does not define the exact parser or shape of adapter output, so formatting depends on the script.

simulations.task: User asks: 'Is memory noisy after the last tool-heavy session?'
simulations.expected_output: Codex would use audit-memory, identify low-value automatic memories or noisy command patterns, report relevant IDs and counts, and recommend archive-noise rather than destructive pruning.
simulations.quality_notes: Strong fit. The skill gives the right command, interpretation frame, and non-destructive recommendation.

simulations.task: User asks: 'Delete stale memory entries and resolve conflicts.'
simulations.expected_output: Codex would not mutate directly under this skill. It would first inspect/gather candidate IDs, then hand mutation work to manage-memory.
simulations.quality_notes: Boundary handling is clear, but complete execution depends on the unavailable manage-memory skill. As standalone instructions, it can correctly stop at inspection and handoff.

scope.assessment: Well-scoped. It covers one coherent domain: inspecting and auditing local RECALL memory. It includes broad reviews, filters, quality checks, ID gathering, and cleanup recommendations without taking over mutation or retrieval-by-topic work. It is not perfect because it includes several related routes and lifecycle command names, which slightly expands the surface beyond pure review, but the core boundary remains clear.
